reading.name: Vietnam
reading.headline: Vietnam is in the Moderate tier (32/100, 144th riskiest of 203; 12th of 36 in East Asia & Pacific). Broadly functional, with specific weak spots.
reading.ground: Most things work most of the time, but there are soft spots: a stretched budget, patchy governance or pockets of unrest. Disruptions happen, and are usually contained and short.

drivers.label: Governance & Institutions
drivers.ground: Institutions you can't rely on: slow or biased courts, demands for bribes, rules that change without warning, weak protection of property and contracts.
drivers.felt_by: Businesses, investors and NGOs dealing with officials, permits, contracts or courts.
evidence: limited political freedoms and accountability (34.5 WGI score, 0–100)

warnings.label: Thin FX reserves (<3 months of imports)
warnings.meaning: The central bank has little foreign currency left: less than three months of imports. Import restrictions, dollar shortages, capital controls or a devaluation often follow.
warnings.response: Firms keep extra stock of imported inputs, convert local earnings to hard currency promptly, and check the rules on moving money out of the country.

direction: Over the longer run it has been fairly stable (36 in 2015, 32 now).

business: Use the score to decide where to look closer: compare with peers (Peers tab) and read the drivers before deciding anything.
Protect against currency and payment risk: price in hard currency or index to inflation, shorten payment terms, consider hedging, and check the rules on moving money out.
Thin reserves often come before import limits or a devaluation: hold extra stock of imported inputs and convert local earnings promptly.
ngo: A development setting: focus on long-term programmes and local partners.
travel: Check your government's official travel advice for Vietnam before you go. It changes far faster than annual data.
Bring more than one way to pay: cash shortages, card problems and fast-changing prices are possible.
research: Start with the drivers: Governance & Institutions carries the most risk. Explain why.
Put it in context: Vietnam ranks 12th of 36 in East Asia & Pacific and the Peers tab shows who is close.
Check whether changes are real: governance moves inside the WGI confidence intervals may be noise (Data tab, Governance).
Test the drivers: the What-if simulator shows which indicators would move the score most.
Write it up: the Assessment builder turns this into a structured brief with probabilities.

caveats: Scores are relative: they show where a country sits among the others and give no probability of any event.
The data look backwards: governance scores describe last year and conflict data lag by up to two years. Check current news and official travel advice.
This is general, educational guidance. It is not investment, legal or security advice.
